images.title: Reflect to straighten the path
images.purpose: Show that reflecting C in line l turns B to A to C into a straight line from B to C′, crossing l at the best A.
images.composition: A horizontal mirror line with B and C below, the reflected point C′ above, and one straight dashed path.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, the main figure large and centred with generous empty margins on all sides, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills, nothing else in the frame. A long horizontal line labelled 'l', drawn in #6B7280. Below it, 3 units down, points B (left) and C (right) 8 units apart on a thin grey line BC labelled '8 cm'. Point C′ directly above C, 3 units above l, joined to C by a thin dotted grey vertical with two matching tick marks showing C to l equals l to C′, and one '3 cm' label on the lower part. A straight dashed #CC79A7 line from B to C′ labelled '10 cm'; where it crosses l is point A, a #CC79A7 dot, exactly above the midpoint of BC. A solid #0072B2 segment from A to C. Point labels 'A', 'B', 'C', 'C′'. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The shortest path is the straight line to the reflection, so the best A sits above the middle of BC.
images.description: Show that reflecting C in line l turns B to A to C into a straight line from B to C′, crossing l at the best A.
images.context: Concept T4.C3x; one image showing only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: BC′ = √(8² + 6²) = 10, so the least AB + AC is 10 cm.

image_decisions.why: The reflection argument only lands when the straight line to C′ is seen; words alone do not make it visible.
